sections.overview: Pseudantechinus bilarni is a small dasyurid marsupial native to northern Australia.
sections.identification: It can be confused with P. mimulus in camera-trap records; recent work warns that the two are similar in appearance.
sections.habitat: It is associated with rocky habitats in the Northern Territory; a 2021 camera-trap record extended its known range at Mittiebah.
sections.diet: The sources used here do not establish a species-specific prey list.
sections.behavior: The recent record was obtained by camera trap; it does not by itself establish a daily activity pattern.
sections.reproduction: The field study used here does not report reproductive observations.
sections.ecology: It occurs in the same broad northern region as P. mimulus, but the two are reported as allopatric in parts of the Northern Territory.
sections.conservation: The Mammal Diversity Database reports Near Threatened globally.
